questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I loved exploring GB and Ireland. They have some amazing hitten cities and national parks, which are very accessible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My favorite part was traveling, the academic stuff wasn't that great.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We had 2 orientation days, where we only got information of the University and campus and multiple tours.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Global Opportunity department gave us a lot of information when we arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Volunteering students at Global Opportunity was so sweet and available throughout the semester as well for questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different halls and buildings have housing at various areas on the campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Every floor/apartment/section had there own kitchen, with everything you would need in that kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Horwood Hall is a place for young people (18 +/-) who wants to do a lot of partying and can stand to live in a mess. Lindsey Hall is nice if you choose the more expensive rooms, the cheaper ones are a bit dirty.
I would recommend Barnes Hall shared house and flat. In this hall you are almost guaranteed to live with other internationals, and it is more cozy, less noise, and overall a nice place to live. People make great friends with their roomates there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived at Horwood Hall, and it was very dirty (the kitchen was disgusting), and I lived with a bunch of 18-year-olds (I'm 25) whom loved to party in the hall all night... So not a great match.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Global Opportunity department are slow to respond to e-mails and often forgets to answer.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First I send a list of all the courses I found interesting. If found these courses on Keele's webpage, although there isn't a lot of information on the courses (If you compare them to KU). Then I was told to choose a top 4 of all the courses I wanted. Afterwards I was told a lot of the courses was not available in the spring semester, eventhough Keele Uni's website said it was. Then I got a list of what was available and I chose from that list. 
2 weeks before arriving I got a lot more info on my courses. 1 week before arriving I was told I was enrolled at the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Global Opportunity department was also in charge of registration of classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I signed up for, but not the classes I originally wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you get a list from Global opportunity of all the courses available to you from the start. It might safe some time. And be patient with them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were all level 7 courses, although not very academic when compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more in-class participation and group work compared to UCPH. Furthermore, not many lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LSC-40055 Infectious Diseases
LSC-40033 Advanced Laboratory Techniques
LSC-40030 Project Management and Business Planning

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked "Project Management and Business Planning" as I got to practice my English skills both literary and verbal with presentations and assignments. 
"Advanced Laboratory Techniques" is the easiest class I have ever taken.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot on food, because my kitchen was so disgusting at Horwood Hall.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is less expensive normally, but the Coop on campus is more expensive than normal supermarkets. 
The train tickets weren't that bad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything. Go check out clubs and societies on Keele's own webpage.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the squash and cricket. I loved it! There are so many clubs so I would recommend joining on of them, even though sports clubs are a bit more expensive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Wales! The small towns by the sea are so charming and Snowdonia national park is so beautiful.
Scottish highlands are also amazing, so rent a car a go expolore.
Got to Ireland on saint Patrick's day... but don't go to Dublin (only Americans there)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People are more friendly, but it might seem a bit frightening and weird at first.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your class and join a sports club. The sports clubs also have a lot of socials which apparently are great and a good way to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Random people talking to you. The Northern English accent can be challenging to understand.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join a sports club.
Go explore the country side/ Go on hikes.
Go to Wales.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The best housing is at Barnes.
People at Keele University and other exchange students are typically around ages of 19-21.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Making great international and local friends.
Visition so much beautiful nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I wasn't to happy about my accommodation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
